brief: Goldman's industrials/materials desk opens with morning macro color (Brazil's Bolsonaro surprise lead lifting local markets, Spain's snap election and France's fiscal uncertainty weighing on the Euro and French equities) then turns to breadth. Aerospace's prior macro-agnostic buy-the-dip view has evolved to stock-specific because the Middle East conflict is now 7-8 months in and jet fuel stays elevated, unlike March when there was still time to adjust; OEM length has proven frustrating. Owned names include BA, RBC, CRS, ATI, DPC with warming to HONA; WWD and HWM are debated; TDG, HEI, TXT underowned. Defense primes have traded poorly despite risk-off conditions; a midterm blue-wave outcome is an overhang and SPCX lock-up expirations add pressure. Investors are more positive LMT/GD, mixed RTX, negative NOC/LHX. GS Economics expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% (vs 33% in Q2 ex-distortions), driven over 50% by AI infrastructure beneficiaries alongside 116% hyperscaler capex growth, with most companies still beating despite the median stock's growth slowing from 14% to 9% on cost pressure and a smaller dollar tailwind. DAL reports Friday with a 6% implied move and consensus below its EPS guide; RPM reports Tuesday with a 4% implied move against very low sentiment.
